topics.label: Cancer therapy framing and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience and sets out the lecture's subject and learning objectives before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Surgery and radiotherapy as local cancer treatments
topics.groupedBecause: They focus on local treatment of a tumour, aiming to remove a confined mass or damage it in place, with early detection and accessibility shaping success.

topics.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy: benefits, toxicity and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cytotoxic drugs damage proliferating cells and consider the treatment's benefits alongside its toxicity and resistance problems.

topics.label: Targeting hormone-dependent cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These treatments block hormone-receptor signaling in cancers that remain dependent on estrogen or androgen for growth.

topics.label: Exploiting cell-cycle checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: Both subtopics show how loss of cell-cycle checkpoint function can be exploited as a cancer-cell vulnerability.

topics.label: PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cancers
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how PARP inhibition creates lethal DNA damage selectively in BRCA-deficient cells that cannot repair the resulting double-strand breaks.

topics.label: Oncogene-targeted therapies and kinase inhibitor limitations
topics.groupedBecause: They trace the identification of oncogenic drivers into targeted kinase treatment and examine the selectivity and resistance problems that follow.

topics.label: Antibody-based cancer therapies
topics.groupedBecause: Their shared logic is to use antibody recognition of cell-surface proteins to make treatment depend on the presence of a chosen target on the cell.

topics.label: Evidence for immune surveillance against cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the proposed role of the immune system in controlling cancer and the evidence and limitations behind that idea.

topics.label: Immune checkpoint inhibition and tumour neoantigens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how checkpoint blockade can reactivate T cells and how tumour neoantigens help determine their response.

topics.label: T-cell-engaging and engineered cell therapies
topics.groupedBecause: Both approaches direct T cells toward tumour cells, either by bridging the cells with a bispecific molecule or by equipping T cells with a tumour-recognizing receptor.

topics.label: Assessing cancer-treatment progress and future choices
topics.groupedBecause: These concluding subtopics consider how well cancer is being controlled, why outcomes and treatment decisions remain challenging, and what those challenges mean for future care.
